rows.subtopic: Probability with Cards, Dice and Coins
rows.stem: Three coins are tossed together. The probability of getting exactly one head, is :
rows.solution:
Tossing three coins gives 8 equally likely outcomes: HHH, HHT, HTH, THH, HTT, THT, TTH, TTT.

Exactly one head occurs in HTT, THT and TTH, that is 3 outcomes.

\(P = \dfrac{3}{8}\), which is option (D) \(\dfrac{3}{8}\).

\(\cot 30^\circ = \sqrt{3}\), so \(\cot^2 30^\circ = 3\), and \(\sec 60^\circ = 2\), so \(\sec^2 60^\circ = 4\).

\(\dfrac{1}{3} \times 3 - \dfrac{1}{2} \times 4 = 1 - 2 = -1\), which is option (A) \(-1\).

rows.subtopic: Number of Tangents from an External Point
rows.stem: PA and PB are tangents to a circle centred at O. If \(\angle PBA = 65^\circ\), then \(\angle APB\) equals :
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - the circle with centre O, the tangents PA and PB, the chord AB and the radii OA and OB; no angle is marked, and the stem states the only value needed. Page idx 8.
rows.solution:
Tangents from an external point are equal, so \(PA = PB\), and in triangle PAB the angles opposite these sides are equal: \(\angle PAB = \angle PBA = 65^\circ\).

The angles of triangle PAB add up to \(180^\circ\), so \(\angle APB = 180^\circ - 2 \times 65^\circ = 50^\circ\).

This is option (C) \(50^\circ\).

rows.stem: Two right triangles PRQ and PSQ are drawn on the same hypotenuse PQ. If PR and QS intersect at T, prove that \(ST \times TQ = PT \times TR\).
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - the two right triangles on the common base PQ, right angles marked at S and R, with PR and QS crossing at T; the stem states the configuration in full. Page idx 14.
rows.solution:
In triangle PSQ the right angle is at S, so \(\angle PST = 90^\circ\) (T lies on SQ). In triangle PRQ the right angle is at R, so \(\angle QRT = 90^\circ\) (T lies on PR).

In triangles STP and RTQ:

\(\angle PST = \angle QRT = 90^\circ\), and \(\angle STP = \angle RTQ\) (vertically opposite angles).

So \(\Delta STP \sim \Delta RTQ\) (AA similarity), and their corresponding sides are proportional:

\(\dfrac{ST}{RT} = \dfrac{TP}{TQ}\), that is \(\dfrac{ST}{TP} = \dfrac{RT}{TQ}\).

Cross-multiplying, \(ST \times TQ = PT \times TR\).

rows.subtopic: Volume of a Combination of Solids
rows.stem: 1000 small thermocol balls of radius \(0{\cdot}5\) cm are kept in a spherical balloon of radius 20 cm. Find the volume of air in the balloon.
rows.solution:
Volume of air in the balloon \(=\) volume of the balloon \(-\) volume of the 1000 thermocol balls

\(= \dfrac{4}{3} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times (20)^3 - 1000 \times \dfrac{4}{3} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times (0{\cdot}5)^3\)

\(= \dfrac{4}{3} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times (8000 - 125) = \dfrac{4}{3} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 7875 = 33000\ \text{cm}^3\).

The volume of air in the balloon is \(33000\ \text{cm}^3\).

rows.subtopic: Section Formula and Ratio of Division
rows.stem: A point P divides the line segment joining the points \(A(-3, 5)\) and \(B(7, -4)\) in a certain ratio. If the point P lies on the line \(y = 2x\), then find the ratio AP : PB and coordinates of point P.
rows.solution:
Let P divide AB in the ratio \(AP : PB = k : 1\). By the section formula,

\(P = \left(\dfrac{7k - 3}{k + 1}, \dfrac{-4k + 5}{k + 1}\right)\).

P lies on the line \(y = 2x\), so

\(\dfrac{-4k + 5}{k + 1} = 2 \times \dfrac{7k - 3}{k + 1}\), that is \(-4k + 5 = 14k - 6\), so \(18k = 11\) and \(k = \dfrac{11}{18}\).

The required ratio is \(AP : PB = 11 : 18\).

Then \(P = \left(\dfrac{7 \times 11 - 3 \times 18}{11 + 18}, \dfrac{-4 \times 11 + 5 \times 18}{11 + 18}\right) = \left(\dfrac{77 - 54}{29}, \dfrac{-44 + 90}{29}\right) = \left(\dfrac{23}{29}, \dfrac{46}{29}\right)\).

(Check: \(\dfrac{46}{29} = 2 \times \dfrac{23}{29}\), so P is on \(y = 2x\).)

rows.stem: A vertical tower stands on a horizontal plane and is surmounted by a vertical flagstaff. From a point on the ground 30 m away from the tower, wires are attached to the top and bottom of the flagstaff making angles of elevation \(60^\circ\) and \(30^\circ\) respectively. Find the height of the tower and lengths of the wires attached. (Take \(\sqrt{3} = 1{\cdot}73\))
rows.solution:
Let AB be the tower of height h m and BC the flagstaff on top of it, and let D be the point on the ground with \(AD = 30\) m. The wire DB to the bottom of the flagstaff makes \(30^\circ\) with the ground, and the wire DC to the top makes \(60^\circ\).

In right triangle BAD:

\(\dfrac{h}{30} = \tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\), so \(h = \dfrac{30}{\sqrt{3}} = 10\sqrt{3} = 10 \times 1{\cdot}73 = 17{\cdot}3\).

The height of the tower is \(17{\cdot}3\) m.

Let the wire to the bottom of the flagstaff be \(l_1\). In the same triangle,

\(\dfrac{30}{l_1} = \cos 30^\circ = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\), so \(l_1 = \dfrac{60}{\sqrt{3}} = 20\sqrt{3} = 20 \times 1{\cdot}73 = 34{\cdot}6\).

Let the wire to the top of the flagstaff be \(l_2\). In right triangle CAD,

\(\dfrac{30}{l_2} = \cos 60^\circ = \dfrac{1}{2}\), so \(l_2 = 60\).

The wire attached to the bottom of the flagstaff is \(34{\cdot}6\) m long and the wire attached to the top is 60 m long.

rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.subtopic: Graphical Method and Nature of Solutions
rows.stem:
Solve the following system of equations graphically :

\(2x + 3y = 5, \quad -3x + y = -2\)
rows.solution:
Points on \(2x + 3y = 5\):

| \(x\) | \(-2\) | 1 | 4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| \(y\) | 3 | 1 | \(-1\) |

Points on \(-3x + y = -2\), that is \(y = 3x - 2\):

| \(x\) | 0 | 1 | 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| \(y\) | \(-2\) | 1 | 4 |

Plot both sets of points on the same axes and draw the two lines. They meet at the point \((1, 1)\).

The solution is \(x = 1\), \(y = 1\). (Check: \(2 + 3 = 5\) and \(-3 + 1 = -2\).)

rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.subtopic: Consistency from the Ratios of Coefficients
rows.stem:
The sum of the digits of a 2-digit number is 11. The number obtained by interchanging its digits exceeds the given number by 9. To know the number :

(i) form the linear equations representing the above situation.

(ii) verify that the equations have a unique solution.

(iii) solve the equations to get the given 2-digit number.
rows.solution:
Let the digit in the units place be x and the digit in the tens place be y, so the number is \(10y + x\).

(i) The sum of the digits is 11: \(x + y = 11\) ... (1)

Interchanging the digits gives \(10x + y\), which exceeds the number by 9:

\(10x + y = 10y + x + 9\), so \(9x - 9y = 9\), that is \(x - y = 1\) ... (2)

(ii) Here \(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} = \dfrac{1}{1} = 1\) and \(\dfrac{b_1}{b_2} = \dfrac{1}{-1} = -1\). Since \(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} \neq \dfrac{b_1}{b_2}\), the lines intersect in exactly one point, so the equations have a unique solution.

(iii) Adding (1) and (2): \(2x = 12\), so \(x = 6\), and then \(y = 11 - 6 = 5\).

The given number is \(10 \times 5 + 6 = 56\). (Check: \(5 + 6 = 11\), and \(65 - 56 = 9\).)
